title: put on your shoes put your shoes on (phrasal verbs 2)
subtitle: put on your coat / put your coat on / put it on
summary: Learn where the object goes with phrasal verbs like put on and take off, and remember that it and them always go in the middle.

lesson.heading: Two places for the object
lesson.text: Sometimes a phrasal verb (**put on** / **take off** etc.) has an object. The object can go after the phrasal verb or in the middle. Both are correct.

examples.text: It was cold, so I **put on** my coat.
examples.note: or I put my coat on.

examples.text: I'm going to **take off** my shoes.

lesson.heading: it and them go in the middle
lesson.text: But **it/them** (pronouns) always go before **on/off** etc. We say **put it on**, not ~~put on it~~, and **take them off**, not ~~take off them~~.

examples.text: Your shoes are dirty. **Take them off**.

lesson.heading: Three ways to say the same thing
turn on / turn off, switch on / switch off
lesson.text: We **turn on** and **turn off** lights, machines and taps. You can also say **switch on** and **switch off** for lights and machines.

examples.text: It was dark, so I **turned on** the light.
examples.note: or I turned the light on.

examples.text: I don't want to watch this programme. You can **turn it off**.
I **switched on** the light and **switched off** the television.

lesson.heading: pick up / put down, bring back / take back / give back
lesson.text: **pick up** = take something up from the floor or a table. **put down** = put something on the floor or a table. **bring/take/give/put ... back** = return something.

examples.text: Those are my keys on the floor. Can you **pick them up** for me?
I stopped reading and **put** my book **down**.
You can take my umbrella, but please **bring it back**.
I've got Rachel's keys. I have to **give them back** to her.
I read the letter and then **put it back** in the envelope.

lesson.heading: More phrasal verbs with an object
rows: write your details on a form
find a word in a dictionary
put clothes on to see if they are the right size
stop a cigarette or a fire burning
make something fall on its side
make a radio or a TV less loud

lesson.text: Never put *it* or *them* at the end: *Put it on*, not ~~put on it~~.

exercises.explanation: A coat is one thing, so we say it - and it goes before on.

exercises.prompt: Your shoes are dirty. Take ___ off.
exercises.explanation: Shoes are more than one thing, so we say them - and them goes before off.

exercises.prompt: I don't want to watch this programme. You can ___
exercises.explanation: it always goes before off: turn it off.

exercises.prompt: Which sentences are correct and which are wrong?

exercises.statement: Those are my keys on the floor. Can you pick up them for me?
exercises.explanation: Can you pick them up for me? The pronoun them goes before up.

exercises.prompt: The sentence is 'He put on his jacket.' Say the same thing with his jacket in the middle.
exercises.explanation: The object can also go in the middle: put his jacket on.

exercises.prompt: My new lamp doesn't work. I'm going to take ___ to the shop.
exercises.explanation: take it back = return it to the shop. it goes before back.

exercises.prompt: There were some gloves on the floor, so I picked ___ and put them on the table.
exercises.explanation: them goes before up: picked them up.

exercises.prompt: Thank you for lending me these books. I won't forget to bring ___.
exercises.explanation: bring them back = return them to you.

exercises.prompt: Match each phrasal verb with its meaning.

pairs.right: find a word in a dictionary
write your details on a form
put clothes on to see if they fit

exercises.prompt: 'What does this word mean?' 'Here's a dictionary. You can look ___.'
exercises.explanation: look it up = find it in a dictionary. it goes before up.

exercises.prompt: Somebody gave me a form and told me to fill ___.
exercises.explanation: fill it in = write your details on it. it goes before in.
